_note: The Wild's pack (app/wild_pack.py): the rules, every Johto and Kanto place with its terrain evidence and wild Pokémon by window, the links between places, and each species' active windows. Reference only: your expeditions are Journal rows.

rules._note: The Wild (v2.7, docs/WILD.md): the rules that turn a real place into an expedition, and the estate's year. Every block says its class: mechanic (the games' own rules or data), inferred (Blackthorn's reading of the games) or creative (a Blackthorn-world model, editable, never canon). wilderness/expedition.py and its browser copy (app/web/41_wild.html) only evaluate them; app/test_wild_parity.mjs holds the two together. The capability needs reuse capability/model.json's ids; the capability engine (capability/assess.py) does the assessing.

aliases._note: landscape places whose encounter area has another name in the tables

windows._note: HeartGold and SoulSilver's clock: morning 4:00-10:00, day 10:00-20:00, night 20:00-4:00. Wild Pokémon tables change with it.

seasons._note: The Gen IV games have no seasons. Blackthorn's world has the four, read from your date the way the rest of the app reads it (spring March-May, summer June-August, autumn September-November, winter December-February).

climate._note: The weather mix for a day outside at a place: weights by its elevation and the season, plus what its biomes add. Inside a cave, a tower or ruins the weather doesn't reach: a place that is only those is 'sheltered' every day.

sheltered.name: Sheltered
sheltered.says: under rock, out of the weather

terrain._note: What a place calls for, as capability needs (capability/model.json ids) with a priority and a reason. Three sources, each kept apart: its biome and elevation (the landscape's reading of it, class inferred; the needs that follow are creative), the game's own encounter methods there (class mechanic: Pokémon on the water means water to cross, Rock Smash encounters mean breakable rocks), and the way there (the games' own map links, class mechanic).
always: hurts away from a Pokémon Center

ice-cave: an ice cave stays below freezing
warmth on the ice, and water from it
deep passages away from the entrance
cave: deep passages away from the entrance
a way out fast if it goes wrong
sea-cave: the passages flood with the tide
sacred-pool: the pool is the way in
alpine: rock and ice above the tree line
forest: no sky to steer by under the canopy
woodland-edge: berries and roots at the woods' edge
grassland: seeds and berries in the grass

methods._note: Encounter methods in the game's own tables at the place, and what each one shows about the ground. A field move here is the game's (cartridge readiness checks it).

surf.why: the game has wild Pokémon on the water here: water to cross

rock-smash.why: breakable rocks (Rock Smash encounters in the game)

headbutt.why: trees to shake (Headbutt encounters in the game)

old-rod.why: fish in the water (the game's rods catch here)

good-rod.why: fish in the water (the game's rods catch here)

super-rod.why: fish in the water (the game's rods catch here)

route._note: The links between places on the games' own map (biology/johto.json, kanto.json, from the HeartGold decomp). A sea link means water to cross; a cave link means a passage underground; rail and ship are the Magnet Train and the S.S. Aqua.
sea: the way there crosses open water

fly.why: flown to the town nearest the place, then on foot

hazards._note: What can go wrong on a day out, when it can happen, and what handles it. A hazard comes up when its weather is drawn or its ground is there; it's handled when the team (or its kit) is ready on every capability it needs, strained when one is only teachable, plausible or waiting for your approval, and a setback when one is a gap.

list.name: Blizzard
list.says: a blizzard pinned the camp down

list.name: Storm
list.says: a storm tore at the camp

list.name: Darkness underground
list.says: the passages went dark past the entrance

sim._note: The optional run (spec §9, 'an optional simulation layer'): a seeded day-by-day field journal from the rules above and the game's own encounter tables. It's a way to see a plan's odds, never canon: run it as often as you like. One wild encounter is drawn per window per day from that window's table: on land, or, when the team can travel on water and the place has Pokémon on it, on the water a third of the time (water_weights). A team turns back after this many setbacks, or when the food runs out.

estate._note: The estate's year and stores (creative unless a line says otherwise).
estate._berry_rations: a picked berry feeds one ration (creative: Blackthorn's standard, capability/model.json → provisions)
estate._growth: mechanic: Gen IV berry growth, from PokeAPI (berries.growth_time is the hours of each of its four stages; max_harvest is the most a plant gives with ideal watering)

outdoor._note: creative: how the season treats a resident outdoors in the highlands, by its type-driven climate (ranch/habitat.py: warm for Fire, cold for Ice, any otherwise)

outdoor_says.shade: needs shade and the cold vault's chill in the heat
outdoor_says.indoors: lives by the hearth until spring
